title: Comparison of Holmium Laser Enucleation of the Prostate (HoLEP) versus MOSESTM Laser Enucleation of the Prostate (MoLEP) in Benign Prostate Syndrome (BPS) - a prospective randomized non-inferiority study
summary:
The aim of this study is to compare two different laser pulse settings approved for laser enucleation of the prostate. The aim here is to verify that the newer MoLEP technology is not inferior to the previous gold standard of HoLEP. The two surgical procedures do not differ in the surgical method, but only in the use of a different laser pulse setting with a special laser fiber.
The surgical principle of MOSES Laser Enucleation of the Prostate (MoLEP) is identical to that of HoLEP. A conventional holmium laser is used in HoLEP. The MoLEP uses a patented technology that aims to improve the energy transfer through the use of a special pulse modulation of the laser. Significant advantages have so far been proven, especially in the treatment of urinary stones. For the treatment of BPH, MOSES technology could also prove beneficial compared to the traditional holmium pulse. Improvements through MoLEP have been reported so far, especially with regard to the operating time due to greater efficiency in enucleation and hemostasis. The improved haemostatic effect is said to improve visibility during enucleation and reduce blood loss during the operation. Postoperative catheter removal may be possible earlier due to a shorter duration of flushing of the bladder.
In the studies available to date, MoLEP has been shown to be equivalent to HoLEP in terms of functional results and the occurrence of complications. However, these studies only retrospectively evaluated data from relatively few patients, so that a large knowledge gap regarding the use of the different laser pulse settings could be closed with the currently planned prospective study. As part of this study, we would like to collect your functional results before and after the operation, as well as the safety profile of laser enucleation.

interventions.name: Patients receive the classic HoLEP as a surgical procedure.
The patients receive the new MoLEP as a surgical procedure.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Indication for subvesical deobstruction
Exclusion criteria:
Prostate less than or equal to 30ccm, urethral stricture, punch biopsy confirmed carcinoma of the prostate, preoperative evidence of prostate carcinoma, neurogenic bladder emptying disorder
